newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher despite late break.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher despite late break.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher, but a late break pulled prices off their earlier highs, traders said.

MGE spring wheat gained throughout the session on spillover from other wheat markets, which climbed on a mixture of fund buying and concern over damage from the cold weather expected in the central U.S. Plains. Spring wheat also drew support from a lack of hedge-selling, traders said.
But values eroded as Country Hedging and LFG each sold about one million March bushels. Traders said most of the selling came in the session's last 45 minutes.
MGE spring wheat settled one to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 3-1/2 cents at $3.84. Earlier, March had set an intraday high at $3.91, up 10-1/2 cents.
Apart from Country Hedging and LFG, other players included CIS, which bought 800,000 March. Atwood-Peavey bought 500,000 March and 500,000 May, traders said.
MGE barley futures closed steady to four cents per cwt higher, with March up four cents at $6.65.
